# Every authorization gate in core and the catalogue action(s) it maps to.
# Checked by coverage_test.go: every action exists, every catalogue action is
# cited, every file exists, and each file has one "group" row per
# RequireRole( / RequireCan( / RequireOwnerOrKeyScope( line in internal/admin and
# internal/server (a new gate needs a row, and an action if none fits).
#
# <backend-relative path> group|inline|flag|other <action>[,<action>...] [roles=<owner|owner,editor>] [n=<count>]   # <note, with line numbers as hints>
#
# roles  = who the check lets through today, for a signed-in session; required
#          on every row but other. authz.Default() must answer the same for
#          an owner and an editor for every cited action (checked by
#          coverage_test.go). Where a plugin's own role list narrows editors,
#          roles is the widest answer and the note says so. It names the staff
#          roles only: the author, contributor, reviewer and read-only roles
#          pass just the actions in authz.readRights plus their content rules (contentRights; see default.go).
#
# group  = a RequireRole / RequireCan / RequireOwnerOrKeyScope line (counted by the test)
# inline = any other gate: an owner/editor check in a handler, a key scope
#          check, or a route open to every signed-in user
# flag   = an owner/editor check that only changes what a screen shows
#          (capability flag, banner, nav); no 403 of its own
# other  = an owner/editor check that is not an access decision (recipient
#          selection, claims derivation); the action column is "-"
#
# Role checks in internal/admin and internal/server are counted per file: the
# optional n=<count> field on inline, flag and other rows is the number of
# lines in that file that compare a role with owner/editor or call requireOwner
# (RequireRole lines are counted by the group rows). The n values of a file
# must add up to the count in the source, so a new check needs a row. Line
# numbers in the notes are hints only. Rows without n= are converted call
# sites: they ask authz.Can (or a helper over it) and keep no inline role check.

# --- admin: RequireRole groups ---
